- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

3	
4	// A PACK'S CONTENT IS DELIVERED ON ITS VERSION NUMBER, and on nothing else. The
5	// engine tree vendors wholesale on every converge; a pack's directory ships only
6	// where `planPackUpdates` sees `installed.packVersions[id] < pack.version`
7	// (updates/pack-update.mjs). So a canon commit that edits `packs/<id>/` without
8	// touching that number lands here, goes green here, and reaches no member — the
9	// fleet keeps the old bytes while canon believes the change shipped.
10	//
11	// #939 is what that costs. A check vocabulary rename updated the engine and the
12	// canon's own packs in one commit: the engine, delivered unconditionally, reached
13	// every member and rejected the old spelling; the pack carrying the new spelling
14	// stayed at `version: 1` and reached nobody. The mixed tree failed each member's
15	// self-test, the update PR parked, and the fix could not arrive by the route that
16	// delivers fixes. Seven repos sat frozen for five days.
17	//
18	// So the invariant this rule holds is one line: A CHANGE UNDER `packs/<id>/` IS A
19	// CHANGE TO THAT PACK'S VERSION. Every SHIPPING byte counts, because every one of
20	// them rides the same directory copy — prose, a skill, a check module, a migration
21	// record. A pack's tests sit beside the files they cover and are the one thing in
22	// that directory no vendor set carries (compute-vendor-set drops `*.test.mjs`), so
23	// nobody is waiting on them and a bump for one would re-deliver every pack in the
24	// tree to say nothing.
25	// It is the pack-side twin of `engine-release-record` (the claudinite local pack),
26	// which holds the same line for `ENGINE_VERSION`.
27	//
28	// WORK SCOPE: the question is what THIS change did. The tree always contains a
29	// version number; only the diff says whether it moved with the content beside it.
30	const LOCAL_PACKS = '.claudinite/local/packs';
31	
32	// Each pack's version-bump log, next to its manifest — see `versionRecorded`
33	// below for what it must carry once a bump lands.
34	export const VERSIONS_FILENAME = 'VERSIONS.md';
35	
36	// The pack ids a changed-file list touches, in first-seen order. Anchored at
37	// `packs/<id>/` so the canon's own local packs (which vendor nowhere, carry no
38	// version and reach no member) and the tree's own files (`packs/README.md`,
39	// `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`) are outside it by construction. Tests drop out for
40	// the same reason the local packs do: nothing delivers them. `VERSIONS.md` drops
41	// out too — it is the log OF bumps, not content a bump ships, so editing it alone
42	// (recording a bump made elsewhere in the same change, or a wording fix to an old
43	// row) must never itself demand another bump.
44	export function packsTouched(changed) {
45	  const ids = [];
46	  for (const file of changed ?? []) {
47	    if (file.startsWith(`${LOCAL_PACKS}/`) || file.endsWith('.test.mjs') || file.endsWith(`/${VERSIONS_FILENAME}`)) continue;
48	    const m = /^packs\/([^/]+)\//.exec(file);
49	    if (m && !ids.includes(m[1])) ids.push(m[1]);
50	  }
51	  return ids;
52	}
53	
54	// The `version:` a pack manifest declares, or null when it declares none (a
55	// manifest that is absent on one side of the diff, or one the schema check owns).

1	---
2	name: extract-from-conversations
3	description: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
4	---
5	
6	# Extract lessons from a conversation
7	
8	The **dialogue** half of lesson extraction: read one agent ↔ user session — its turns *and* the actions
9	taken in it — and convert its friction into changes that make the **next** run faster, clearer, and less
10	dependent on human steering. Its sibling [extract-from-activity](../extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) mines
11	what the work committed; this one mines how the work went.
12	
13	The **bar** a lesson must clear, the **local promotion ladder** it descends, and where a repo's capture
14	surface lives stay canonical in [extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — read it, don't
15	re-derive it. What follows is only what reading a *conversation* adds.
16	
17	## The goal
18	
19	Every pass optimizes for one outcome: **the next run needs less.** Less clarification, less rework, less
20	waiting, less human steering. Read the session not as "what did we accomplish" but as "where did this
21	cost more than it should have, and what durable change removes that cost next time." If a pass can't name
22	a concrete next-time saving, it found nothing — and that's fine.
23	
24	## Where the conversation comes from
25	
26	- **A captured log** on the repo's orphan `conversation-logs` branch (`<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`),
27	  read with plain git in the checkout — `git show origin/conversation-logs:<file>`. The log carries
28	  per-entry timestamps, per-message token usage, and the `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs behind every
29	  wall-time number, which is exactly what the measured analysis below needs. This is the routine path.
30	- **The live session**, when an owner asks in plain words for a retrospective. Same method; deliver the
31	  capture as a branch + PR **for a human to review**, never one that self-merges.
32	
33	**Never reflect-and-edit unprompted in the middle of a task** — it interrupts the work; the owner decides
34	when a session is done enough to mine.
35	
36	## What to look for — the friction signals
37	
38	Read the conversation end to end and hunt for these signatures. Each marks a place the loop cost more than
39	necessary, and each converts to a specific durable fix.
40	
41	### 1. Misunderstandings between agent and user
42	
43	The signs: a clarifying-question round-trip; the user correcting an assumption ("no, I meant…"); the agent
44	building the wrong thing and reworking it; the user restating the same request; an `AskUserQuestion` whose
45	answer was, in hindsight, the obvious default.
46	
47	**Convert to:** encode the resolved understanding so the next agent never has to ask. Every question the
48	user answered is a candidate **default**; every correction is a candidate **convention or glossary entry**;
49	a recurring wrong assumption is a candidate **confirm-first checkpoint placed earlier**, or a clearer doc
50	the agent reads cold and gets right the first time. The test of a good fix: next time the agent proceeds
51	correctly **without the round-trip**.
52	
53	### 2. Suboptimal agent actions
54	
55	The signs: the agent took an approach then backtracked; did redundant or repeated work; re-ran a command
56	that had already failed for a knowable reason; reached for a heavy tool where a light one fit; reinvented
57	something the codebase already provided; re-read a file it had just written to "verify"; missed an existing
58	convention and had it corrected in review.
59	
60	**Convert to:** a rule pointing at the right approach or tool, a pointer to the existing helper/convention
61	so it's found first, or a **footgun note placed where it'll be read** (the usage-site-vs-central call is in
62	[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md)). The test: next time the agent takes the good path
63	first, not after a detour.
64	
65	### 3. Long wall-time waits — and measure them
66	
67	The signs: independent operations run **serially** that had no dependency and could have been parallel; a
68	padded fixed `sleep` that over- or under-shot; a process **waited out after its result was already in
69	hand**; blind long polling; re-running a check (e.g. CI) that was already green.
70	
71	**Measure, don't hand-wave.** Quantify the wait with real wall-clock numbers from the log's own timestamps
72	and separate the kinds of time — compute (a compile, a test/render run) vs. genuine **idle waiting**
73	(sleeps, polling, a finished process not yet killed). The numbers are computable, never estimated. A fix is
74	only credible against numbers; name the **single highest-leverage change** that shortens it, or conclude it
75	was already optimal.
76	
77	**Convert to:** a batch/parallelize rule, a poll-with-rolling-backoff instead of a blind sleep,
78	kill-the-process-once-its-output-is-in-hand, or merge-on-an-already-green-check. (These are the subject of
79	the standing **efficiency analysis** in [the unattended-agents skill](../unattended-agents/SKILL.md) — fold
80	a wall-time finding into that frame rather than re-deriving it.) The test: same result, less wall clock, no
81	loss of quality.
82	
83	## Encode the questions the user keeps asking
84	
85	The single highest-leverage move for **less human feedback**: the questions a user asks *repeatedly* are a
86	checklist the agent should run **itself.** If the user keeps asking "how many processes ran — could it be
87	fewer?", "what took longest?", "did you kill it the moment its work was done?", stop waiting to be asked —
88	fold those exact questions into a **standing self-check the agent answers proactively** at the end of the
89	relevant work, and close with a terse verdict (a concrete change, or an explicit "already optimal"). Each
90	recurring question converted this way is one the user never has to ask again — and it's where a *measured*
91	retrospective comes from: the user's recurring efficiency questions, answered pre-emptively, with numbers.
92	
93	## Two windows per run: the newest day, and the oldest day still on the branch
94	
95	Every run reads exactly two sets of captures, both taken from the filename stamps:
96	
97	- **the last 24 hours** — the fresh pass, over what was captured since the previous run;
98	- **the first 24 hours on the branch** — every capture stamped within 24h of the oldest one still there.
99	  This is the hindsight pass, and it is a real re-read rather than a formality: a friction signal that
100	  looked situational when it was fresh may have recurred since, and a lesson landed since may have made a
101	  keeper redundant. Both directions are legitimate outcomes, and corpus dedup makes the overlap harmless.
102	
103	The two windows are also what keeps deletion honest. Retention is an agentless task that prunes on the
104	stamp alone, with no handshake back to this one — safe because the branch is read from its oldest end
105	every run, so a capture reaches retention having been read. Reading less than the oldest window silently
106	breaks that; reading more is only wasted effort.
107	
108	## Provenance: summarize the exchange, never paste it
109	
110	For each rule that actually **lands** from a log, post one short comment on the issue the log names
111	(`--issue-<n>--` in its filename; **`--issue-0--` means the capture had no associated issue**, so there is
112	nothing to post on and the rule simply lands without a comment):
113	
114	- one provenance line — the rule added, the capture date, the session id;
115	- then a **200-word-max** description of just the slice of conversation that caused the rule: what was
116	  asked, what went wrong or got corrected, and why the rule follows from it.
117	
118	**Summarize, never transcribe.** The dialogue itself is far too verbose for an issue — no pasted turns
119	beyond a short quoted phrase, never raw JSONL, never a rendered transcript. A log that yields nothing gets
120	**no** comment: extraction is the only path to permanence, and a log's conversation is gone once retention
121	deletes it. That is a deliberate call, so a padded "lesson" written to feel productive costs more than the
122	silence it replaced.
123

1	# Extracting lessons — the bar and the local promotion ladder
2	
3	> **Scope: what both extraction skills share.** This doc is the **bar** a lesson must clear and the
4	> **ladder** it descends once it clears it — the half that is identical whatever the lesson was mined
5	> from. What each *source* adds is owned by its own skill:
6	> [extract-from-activity](skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) for commits, merged PRs and issue
7	> activity, and [extract-from-conversations](skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md) for a session's
8	> dialogue. Both load this doc; neither restates it.
9	
10	Its callers are the growth pack's [growth-extract](tasks/growth-extract/task.md) daily task, which runs
11	both skills over one window, and an owner's occasional plain-words ask for a retrospective.
12	
13	## Run the pass on a capable model
14	
15	Extraction is mechanical, but deciding *what clears the bar* is a judgment call a weaker model fails
16	silently — it ships a plausible-but-wrong "lesson" where a capable model correctly bails (see
17	[the unattended-agents skill](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md), "Match the agent model to the judgment it
18	must make"). The terse rules that *govern* the pass — run it, plus the separate efficiency analysis — also
19	live there; this doc is the how-to.
20	
21	## From signal to lesson — the bar
22	
23	A signal is only worth writing down when the fix is **durable, reusable, and generalizable beyond this one
24	session or window.** Before adding anything:
25	
26	- **Dedupe ruthlessly** against the existing packs — a lesson already covered (even worded differently,
27	  even in another pack, even enforced by a check) is not a new lesson.
28	- **A dedupe miss has a second reading**, and when the candidate rule names an identifier you don't
29	  own — a function, field or setting — it is the likelier one: grep that identifier in the
30	  dependency's **code** before landing anything. No hit usually means the mechanism was retired and
31	  the rule is *expired*, not that the lesson is novel.
32	- **One-offs don't qualify.** A situational detail, a restatement of a generic truism, or something already
33	  implied by an existing rule is below the bar.
34	- **Never capture a rule that teaches routing around a permission, security, or classifier denial.** A
35	  pattern of "it was denied, then succeeded on retry" is real signal about *reliability*, not license to
36	  write a rule instructing every future session to retry, ignore, or explain past such a denial without
37	  asking — however solid the retry evidence looks, that shape of lesson never clears the bar. Report a
38	  recurring denial to the owner instead; a checked-in instruction that tells unattended sessions to bypass
39	  a safety gate is a standing bypass with no consent behind it, however it got there.
40	- **Promote what's portable.** A lesson true for projects beyond this one belongs in shared, cross-project
41	  canon, not stuck in one repo's local packs — the growth lifecycle's promote stage lifts it there
42	  centrally; capture it well locally and let promote generalize whatever travels.
43	
44	## Route to the local pack that owns it — the promotion ladder
45	
46	A project's capture surface is its **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/<pack>/`); everything else
47	under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mounted canon and is never a capture target. Pick the pack whose
48	territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack; some segregate a domain pack), then
49	prefer the strongest mechanism it allows:
50	
51	**First check whether a canon pack already owns it, from the catalog and not from the mount.** A repo
52	holds only the packs it *declares*, so "nothing here covers this" is a fact about the mount rather than
53	about the corpus — and acting on it homes the lesson locally in territory a canon pack already owns.
54	Read `.claudinite/shared/packs/directory.GENERATED.md` (canon-side `packs/directory.GENERATED.md`),
55	which states every canon pack's boundary including the ones this repo doesn't hold. Where the owning
56	pack's stated territory is merely too narrow, propose widening it rather than routing around it.
57	
58	1. **A declared check** — an entry in that pack's `declared-checks.json`, whose `failureMessage` *is* the
59	   lesson. Nothing wires it: writing the declaration adds the check. This is the first rung to try for any
60	   lesson whose whole logic is "these patterns over these files", and most captured conditions are. Give it
61	   `severity: 'blocking'` and `since: '<today>'`: the engine holds a check to advisory for its first two
62	   weeks, so a check may land against a tree that still violates it and the backlog it surfaces is somebody
63	   else's next change, not this run's.
64	2. **A custom code rule** — a `<rule>.mjs` exporting `run(ctx)`, listed on the pack's `pack.mjs` — only
65	   when the check needs what patterns can't say: real parsing, structured-data field logic, git/diff or
66	   conversation state, a derived comparison. Reaching for code where a declaration would do costs a module
67	   to read and maintain for nothing. An **unattended** run ships one `advisory`: hand-written logic has
68	   failure modes a declaration cannot have, and nobody reviewed this one.
69	3. **A pack skill**, when the lesson is an activity-scoped procedure rather than a condition.
70	4. **Terse prose** in the pack's `RULES.md` — the fallback, only what none of the above can carry.
71	
72	Either check rung ships with a **red-first fixture**; the declaration vocabulary is documented in
73	[`pattern-rules.mjs`](../../engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs)'s header, and the authoring shape for
74	both rungs — with the `since` grace window — in
75	[`engine/checks/README.md`](../../engine/checks/README.md#adding-a-rule).
76	
77	**Two check shapes are below the bar however cleanly they'd be written**: one that asserts particular code
78	exists or still reads a particular way (it pins a point in time and reds the next legitimate edit), and one
79	derivable from the product's own requirements (that is a requirement — it belongs in the tests).
80	
81	Write **more checks and less prose**: a check relieves every session's context completely, where prose only
82	relocates it. **Prose is rationed, and the ration is small.** Every rule in a `RULES.md` is paid for by every
83	session in every repo that declares the pack, forever, whether or not it ever applies — so a pass adds *at
84	most two*, each one sentence: the trigger, the directive, and a consequence clause only where the rule can't
85	be applied without it. A candidate that needs a paragraph to land has not been understood well enough to be
86	a rule yet; the evidence behind it belongs in the pack's `VERSIONS.md` row and the issue, never in the rule.
87	If more than two candidates clear every bar above, write the two strongest and drop the rest — they will
88	recur if they were real.
89	
90	When no pack's scope fits, the lesson lands in the repo's general local pack. A **new** local
91	pack is justified only by the repo's own **project structure** — a segment of the repo's tree whose work is
92	its own territory (a `client` pack for work under `client/`), so a repo's local packs mirror its layout.
93	**Never mint a local pack around a technology or a methodology**, however real the knowledge: capture those
94	lessons in the structural pack that owns the work, and let the canon-side promote stage — Claudinite's call,
95	never a member's — decide whether a technology or methodology facet earns a pack of its own.
96	
97	**A gotcha tied to one call site is not a pack rule at all, and it is not this pass's to land either.** A
98	trap from misusing a specific API, class, or library belongs as a comment at that usage site — and a capture
99	run's write surface stops at its own packs, so **drop the candidate** rather than inflate it into a pack
100	rule or collect it into a centralized gotchas list. The comments in a repo's own source belong to the
101	tidy-repo pack's `improve-comments` task, which has its own trigger and its own review surface. Reserve a
102	central gotchas doc for what no single usage site owns: a trap you could hit *without* reading the relevant
103	file (a mistake of omission), or a cross-cutting invariant.
104	
105	**Two kinds never become a pack rule, however strong the evidence** — filter on what the lesson is *about*
106	before picking a mechanism. (1) **The owner's own preferences** — which word authorizes a merge, tone, how a
107	summary is shaped. They belong to the person, are injected per session from their own preference file, and
108	change without any repo hearing about it; a pack copy goes stale silently and then contradicts the live one.
109	(2) **The agent framework's own loading mechanics** — which packs are declared, why a skill didn't mount, why
110	an injection missed. That's engine plumbing, not project knowledge: a real defect there is filed upstream, and
111	writing it down as a project rule preserves the bug instead of fixing it.
112	
113	## "No new lessons" is a valid — and common — result
114	
115	Most sessions and most windows yield nothing durable, and that's the expected outcome. Say so and write
116	nothing rather than padding the docs to look productive: a spurious or duplicative "lesson" pollutes the
117	canon and costs every future reader. **Default to no edit when unsure** — the bar is a genuinely new,
118	reusable insight, not a diary of what happened.
119

1	# canon-curation
2	
3	Claudinite's own curation duties — the fleet-facing work only **Claudinite** runs: promoting
4	members' lessons into the shared canon, sweeping the fleet's stacks for technologies the canon does
5	not yet home, and policing the corpus's `packs/` tree. (The
6	prose-to-checks backlog sweep is no longer canon-only — it moved to
7	[claudinite-growth](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/README.md) as a per-repo task with a
8	`pack_paths` config, so every repo sweeps its own packs and Claudinite also its core `packs/`.) A
9	**local pack** of the canon home
10	(`.claudinite/local/packs/`, by owner decision 2026-07-19: Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite is
11	project-specific content, so it lives on the home's own capture surface, not in the portable
12	canon): `detect: null`, never seeded by `--init` or any migration, declared by hand in exactly one
13	repo — the canon home itself, as `local/canon-curation`. Its `tasks/<name>/` folders are found by
14	the home repo's own scheduler exactly like a canon pack's.
15	
16	**Declaration cardinality is the mechanism.** A pack's tasks run once per *declaring* repo, so a
17	pack only the home repo declares yields exactly one work item per task per occurrence — "central,
18	once" with no bespoke orchestrator step. Un-declaring the pack freezes canon absorption without touching
19	the members' side ([claudinite-growth](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/README.md)).
20	
21	| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `growth-promote` | a participating member changed its local packs in the window | a PR against Claudinite's `main` |
24	| `growth-discover-packs` | weekly, over every covered member | a PR against Claudinite's `main`, plus an adopt issue in each member that evidenced the pack |
25	
26	| Rule (≤5 words) | How enforced |
27	|---|---|
28	| Pack prose: no enforcement narration | check `pack-no-enforcement-narration` |
29	| Pack edit bumps pack version | check `pack-version-bumped` |
30	| Packs import only own + engine | declared barrier `pack-independence` ([declared-checks.json](declared-checks.json) — a `forbidReferences` entry; the [barriers pack](../../../../packs/barriers/README.md) documents the edge vocabulary) |
31	
32	- **[tasks/growth-promote/](tasks/growth-promote/task.md)** — the growth lifecycle's central stage: read the changed members'
33	  local packs, **generalize** the portable lessons, route each to the right canon home, and open a
34	  PR for the owner to approve. When a portable lesson's technology has no pack home, it mints a
35	  fingerprinted **stub pack** (in its own dedicated PR). This is the sole judgment gate before
36	  shared canon.
37	- **[tasks/growth-discover-packs/](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)** — the weekly **fleet sweep** for
38	  technologies the canon does not yet home: read every member's stack, fold the members into one view
39	  (so first-sight dedup is free — the third member using a technology is the same gap as the first),
40	  and open an owner-reviewed PR authoring the missing `packs/<tech>/`. A pack is authored because
41	  particular members' files demonstrated it, so each of those members also gets an issue asking it to
42	  adopt the pack once the PR merges and its mount carries it. Its per-repo namesake in
43	  [claudinite-growth](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)
44	  is the other side of that line — it authors a repo's own **local** packs and may never re-create what
45	  a canon pack homes, so only this task can close a canon gap. (Promote's stub-minting is narrower
46	  still: one lesson's technology, minted as a seed; this task authors from the whole fleet's usage.)
47	- **[item-routing.md](item-routing.md)** — the shared worthiness + routing method promote (and an
48	  owner-requested retrospective pass) defers to, so every decision about admitting and placing an
49	  item is made the same way.
50	- **[promote-scope.mjs](promote-scope.mjs)** — the CI write-surface gate on promote's PRs: promote
51	  may write only under `packs/` and `skills/` (keyed on the `growth-promote` branch prefix).
52	
53	## The growth lifecycle — three independent stages, no barriers
54	
55	How a lesson is learned in a consuming project, lifted into the shared canon when it's portable,
56	and pruned back out of the project once the canon owns it. Two packs split it by who declares them:
57	**[claudinite-growth](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/README.md)** (member-side: extract + dedup + pack
58	discovery, seeded, opt-out by removal) and **canon-curation** (this pack, the central stage).
59	
60	```
61	EXTRACT   per member    → auto-merging PR against the member's main   (claudinite-growth)
62	PROMOTE   central, once → PR against Claudinite's main                (canon-curation)
63	DEDUP     per member    → PR against the member's main                (claudinite-growth)
64	```
65	
66	All three are ordinary, **independent** planner units — there is no barrier and no phase ordering.
67	Each stage reads only what is already **merged**: promote processes whatever sits on members' mains
68	when it runs, so a lesson extracted tonight is promoted **tomorrow** night (the extract PR's merge
69	shows up in the next night's local-pack signal), and reaches other members' dedup once the promote PR
70	is approved and merged. That approval was always the dominant latency, so the barrier machinery bought little;
71	if the cadence ever matters, promote can run more often (twice daily, or before and after the
72	nightly) without any design change.
73	
74	**Review gates by blast radius, not uniformly.** Promote opens a PR — it's the sole judgment gate
75	before the shared canon every repo reads, so it always needs a human eye. Dedup opens a PR too — a
76	wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson. Extract lands through an **auto-merging PR** against the
77	member's `main` — it writes only that project's own local packs, so it earns a CI gate and a PR trail
78	but not a human reviewer; auto-merge keeps the fleet's daily lesson-capture from flooding review
79	requests. (An owner-requested, in-session retrospective delivers a PR for a human to review — see
80	[extracting-lessons.md](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/extracting-lessons.md).)
81	
82	**Central execution, no plumbing.** Promote runs from the Claudinite home repo with a fleet-wide
83	token, so it reads every participating member and opens its canon PR directly here — no
84	consumer-side Action, no cross-repo PAT, no labelled-issue up-path. The planner hands its gate the
85	`fleetMembers` aggregate (which members changed, and what they declare), and the gate hands the
86	worker the changed participants as `targets`.
87	
88	**This pack's tasks reach every member, so they name the wider invocation endpoint.** Both tasks
89	here declare `invocation_endpoint: 'fleet'` — a key into this repo's own
90	`taskScheduler.endpoints`, mapping to a routine whose sources are this repo **and every
91	participating member**. That cross-repo reach is the whole reason a second endpoint exists, and is
92	exactly what must stay off the endpoint an ordinary hand-off calls.
93	
94	Reach is a property of **which endpoint is called**, and of nothing else: there is no session scope
95	anywhere in the system, and no label routes a hand-off ([the writing-tasks skill](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/skills/writing-tasks/SKILL.md)).
96	The `session_scope: 'fleet'` these tasks used to declare lost its last reader with the slot
97	scheduler and is gone from both.
98	
99	The failure mode moved with the mechanism, and moved in the right direction. A misconfigured
100	endpoint used to be **silent and permanent**: a dispatch label nothing picked up, re-armed hourly,
101	repeating forever with no comment anywhere. Now the hand-off is a synchronous API call, so an
102	endpoint this repo has not configured — or one whose token secret is unset — converges the item to
103	`needs-human` naming what is missing, on the item itself. If promote or discover-packs has quietly
104	stopped producing anything, read its most recent work item; the reason is written there.
105	
106	The session-scoped sibling of this nightly lifecycle — mining a single working session for lessons
107	— lives with [the growth pack's extract-from-conversations skill](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
108	(applied by the conversation half of its growth-extract daily task over captured logs), and the
109	member-side method docs (extract, dedup, pack discovery, and how a project's local packs are
110	identified) live with [claudinite-growth](../../../../packs/claudinite-growth/README.md).

{"number":1384,"title":"tidy-repo: an improve-comments task and skill","body":"Closes #1383

The comments in a repo's own source were nobody's work. tidy-repo gains a fourth dimension for them — its first task whose subject is the source rather than the repo's GitHub objects — and loses its `RULES.md`.

## The task

`packs/tidy-repo/tasks/improve-comments/` — weekly, gated on a substantive commit in the window, scoped to the files those commits touched (capped at 40, with the remainder named as out of scope rather than silently dropped). It runs the skill and nothing else.

Its precondition also declines while a PR titled `Claudinite tidy: improve comments` is still open, so a second unreviewed sweep is never stacked on the first over files it may already have touched. That is the `wiki-growth` precedent — read from the pending PR itself, so a PR you opened by hand from the branch gates the round too.

`expected_outcome: 'open-pr'`, and I want to flag that choice rather than bury it: the scope gate proves the diff is comment-only, which is what makes the pass safe to run unattended — it says nothing about whether the comments it wrote are *right*, and a confidently wrong comment is the exact failure this task exists to remove. A human reads the words. If you'd rather these land themselves, it is one line in the declaration.

## The skill

`packs/tidy-repo/skills/improve-comments/` — the method. What to fix, in the order the value falls: a comment that says what the code already says (delete — the most common right answer), one that no longer matches the code beneath it, one that narrates the edit that produced it, a dead `TODO`, and a missing why. What to leave alone: a comment you don't understand, a licence header or lint directive, a suppression's inline reason, a published doc comment.

## The gate

`checks.mjs` beside the SKILL.md, blocking, work-scoped, and self-gating on the pass's pinned commit subject — so it is silent on every ordinary branch and costs a declaring repo nothing.

It strips the comments from both sides of every changed file and compares what is left. The permission is **read, never asserted**: a run that quietly renamed a variable while "improving comments" is exactly what this catches, and a run cannot talk its way past a text comparison. Three shapes fail deliberately — a file whose language the parser cannot read counts as code; an added or deleted code file is never comment-only; and a deleted `README.md` is not an improvement to a README.

`commentOnly` and its checkable-extension set move to `engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs` beside the `stripComments` they were already built on, with the queue's narrow-diff classifier and this gate as the two callers.

## The pack loses its `RULES.md`

Its four bullets described what the pack's own workers do, and each worker already states its policy — in more detail — in the `task.md` it loads at run time. So the prose charged every session in every declaring repo for a description of four unattended runs it is never part of. What the policy *is*, for a human reading about the pack, is `README.md`'s job, and that is where it now lives. Seven canon packs already ship without prose, `claudinite-tasks` among them, so this is a well-trodden shape.

Three tests used `tidy-repo` as their stand-in for "a pack with prose" and now name one that has some. The rules index is regenerated by its generator, not hand-edited.

The canon rule that should have caught this named only "a paragraph that explains how a mechanism works". Widened in `.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/RULES.md` to the shape that got past it: anything in a `RULES.md` that describes rather than instructs.

A survey of the other packs found no second case — `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog` is the only other `RULES.md` naming its own tasks, and it is the right shape, opening by saying what the pack *is* belongs in its README and this file is what a session there has to get right.

## Verification

- `packs/tidy-repo/test/skills/improve-comments/checks.test.mjs` — 9 cases. Seen to fail on the four blocking ones with the gate's filter short-circuited.
- Two new rehearsal fixtures (`tidy-repo-member`, fresh and stale) prove a member declaring tidy-repo converges green with the new blocking rule mounted — the `consumer-safe-change` answer, and the honest one here since the rule is additive and inert on any branch that is not this pass.
- Full suite: 2753/2753. `check_the_world` and `check_the_work`: 0 blocking.

{"number":1375,"title":"Plan the convergence as ops; let the session execute its own","body":"`invoke.mjs` hands queue work to Claude Code **web** sessions. `converge-item.mjs` — the last step of every one of those runs — performed its five side effects as a straight line of `await api.…` calls, which silently made REST the only transport. Those sessions have no REST route to their own repository, so the run did its work and then parked looking failed. Fourteen items in `missingbulb/WIP` (missingbulb/WIP#62).

## What the environment actually offers, measured

| Transport | Result |
|---|---|
| `api.github.com/user`, `/rate_limit` | **200**, authenticated as `missingbulb`, 15000/hr |
| `api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/…` | **403** — *"GitHub access is not enabled for this session"* |
| `git` over HTTPS | **works** — the proxy injects credentials; 742 refs listed, pushes succeed |
| MCP GitHub tools | **work** — issues, labels, comments, close |

So REST is not blocked wholesale; repo-scoped paths are gated behind an org-level GitHub App connection. git works but cannot touch issues — they are not refs. **The session's own tools are the access that exists.**

## The change

`convergeOps(item, plan)` is now the single description of what a convergence *is* — an ordered list of comment / record / removeLabel / addLabel / close ops. Two executors consume it:

- **`convergeItem`** applies them over REST. Behaviour unchanged; its 15 existing tests pass untouched.
- **`sessionScript`** renders the same ops as the exact calls a session makes with its own GitHub tools.

The session still supplies nothing but the judgment — which outcome, and the prose. It no longer improvises the transition, because every step is computed for it.

Two differences the session's surface forces, both handled in code rather than left to the session:

- **No granular label write.** `issue_write` replaces the whole set, so the granular removes and adds are folded into the final set, computed from the labels the item was read with — unrelated labels are carried through. For any *other* issue (the legacy shadow write-back) the script emits a read-modify-write naming only the change, never a computed set, because this process never saw that issue's labels.
- **The record is printed by the session**, which is where the census needs it anyway: the usage fold reads `claudinite-task-exec` out of the transcript. This closes a gap the old path had — those fourteen runs are missing from the census permanently.

`instructions.md` gains the session's path through step 6, and fixes the park for a convergence that could not run at all at `task:needs-human-failure` — the only sub-label that **holds the task's lane**, which is why the wrong choice turned one broken convergence into fourteen nightly incidents.

## What this replaces

An earlier revision of this PR deferred convergence to a lodged request the hourly scheduler applied. That was a workaround: it spread one item's completion across three parties and left the real question — *why can't the script reach the repo?* — unasked. It is gone; nothing was added to `scheduler-run.mjs`.

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2750 pass, 0 fail (needs `git fetch --unshallow`; the history-walking shim test fails loudly on a shallow clone by design).
- `check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, nothing advisory on any file this touches. `check_the_work.mjs` — clean.
- 8 new tests, watched failing against two mutations: computing a label set for the foreign issue (1 fail — the bug this caught during development), and not dropping the claim label (4 fail, **including two REST-path tests**, which is what proves the planner is genuinely shared rather than duplicated).

Not in scope: whether convergence should release dependents at all — that is #1373. The REST path still releases them; the session path leaves them to the hourly scheduler, which `readiness.mjs` already documents as the backstop for exactly this.

Closes #1374

{"number":1394,"title":"do-later: teach the skill the queue's Not-before: wait field","body":"Closes #1393

`/do-later` described a deferral's wait as issue-shaped only — previous deferral → open PR → session issue → nothing — so an owner deferring with a *time* ("check tomorrow", "in a week") fell to case 4, and the skill told the session to say the issue "queues immediately". It then did, on the next hourly scheduler run.

The queue has carried the other wait all along. This teaches the skill to use it:

- the body block now shows `Not-before:` beside `Blocked-by:`, and says the two waits compose;
- a new paragraph says what the field is for, that it is the queue's own wait field rather than a request parameter (so it is honoured whether or not the author holds push access, unlike `Task:` / `Model:` / `Automerge:`), what shape the instant takes, and that a time-worded deferral is never the "queues immediately" case;
- the numbered list is retitled "What issue it waits on", since it is now one of two waits.

No engine or queue code changes — the mechanism was already there:

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/work-item.mjs` — `parseRequestFields` returns `notBefore` in both the gated and ungated branches.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, job 2 — `status: blockedBy.length || notBefore ? BLOCKED : READY`, with a past `Not-before` dropped rather than carried.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/readiness.mjs` — `isReleasable` gates on `nowMs >= new Date(notBefore).getTime()`.

## Verification

`parseRequestFields` against a body carrying the field, which is the claim the new prose makes about gating:

ungated: {"task":null,"model":null,"merge":null,"blockedBy":[],"notBefore":"2026-08-28T09:00:00Z","ungated":true}
gated  : {"task":null,"model":"opus","merge":"if-narrow","blockedBy":[],"notBefore":"2026-08-28T09:00:00Z","ungated":false}
```

- `node --test packs/basics/test/pack.test.mjs` — 37 pass, 0 fail.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs` — silent.
- `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs` — 0 blocking, 87 advisory (all pre-existing; none on the edited file).

{"number":1379,"title":"A new check declares when it was added, and is advisory for two weeks","body":"Closes #1378

Per-repo growth capture accumulated long prose rules because the rung above prose was closed to it.

## A grace window on a new check

A check declaration may carry `since: 'YYYY-MM-DD'`, the date it was added, and a `blocking` check is enforced as **advisory** for its first `GRACE_DAYS` (14) from it. Applied in `reportFindings`, the one funnel every runner goes through, before the project's own severity overrides — so a project that sets the rule to `blocking` itself gets enforcement from day one. A rule with no `since` has no grace (absence means mature, never newborn), and a `since` in the future grants nothing, since a date far enough out would be a suppression wearing a creation date. Findings inside the window print the date the rule starts blocking.

This is what removes the bar that forced lessons to prose: `growth-extract`'s doc said a new check must ship green, so the only check a capture run could land was one the tree already satisfied — the check that proves least.

The window is measured from the declared date, not from the day a consumer received the rule, so a canon rule's grace is spent by the time a member converges onto it. A rule going out to the fleet still has to be one the fleet can satisfy; the window only helps the repo that authored it. Stated in `engine/checks/README.md`.

## The prose ration

Prose is rationed at **two one-sentence rules per run**; a candidate needing a paragraph has not been understood well enough to be a rule yet, and the evidence behind it belongs in the pack's `VERSIONS.md` row and the issue. Two check shapes are named below the bar: one that asserts particular code still reads a particular way, and one derivable from the product's own requirements.

A lesson tied to one call site is now **dropped** rather than inflated into a pack rule naming that site. A repo's own comments are not the growth lifecycle's to write — they belong to the tidy-repo pack's `improve-comments` task, landing separately.

**Canon promotion is untouched.** `canon-curation/growth-promote` stays `open-pr`, never arms auto-merge, and already excludes code comments from what it mines.

## Verification

- `engine-tests/check-grace.test.mjs` — 10 tests over the window, the clock injected at every assertion. Seen to fail with `applyGrace` short-circuited.
- Full suite: 2751/2752. The one failure is `engine-pack-lane-shims` refusing to run on a shallow clone — its own guard, unrelated to this change, and identical on `main`.
- `check_the_world` and `check_the_work`: 0 blocking.

{"number":1385,"title":"Label scheme PR 3, re-landed: write the canonical spellings","body":"Stage 3 of #1119 — the write-side flip. **Supersedes #1152**, which cannot merge: `mergeable_state: "dirty"`, 11 content conflicts, and its whole diff was written against `engine/scheduler/queue/`, a directory #1317 has since moved to `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/`. Its green also predated 52 commits on `main`.

The gate #1152 waited on is satisfied. #1154's `Verify:` now passes on all three legs — the two file legs were confirmed fleet-wide on 2026-08-24, and the third (no member parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z citing a label, a status or a missing label) was read this session across all 14 active members. The parks are `converge-item.mjs` auth failures, a missing `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN`, a `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` and one 404 — none of them the label scheme. Full reads: #1119.

## What flips

- **The write constants hold today's spellings** — statuses, terminals, and the origin on every born item. Their *names* survive because fielded pack versions import them: a pack still on the old engine writes a legacy label, which every decoder reads as what it always meant.
- **A park stops being a pair.** `needs-human` + a sub-label could be half-applied — a torn state of its own — so a park is one `task:status:needs-human-`, written by one swap. Executor, session converge, scheduler reclaim and the janitor's sweep all follow.
- **The legacy spellings become explicit `LEGACY_*` literals.** The decode map was built from the constants that just moved; left alone it would have mapped today's spelling to itself and forgotten the vocabulary it exists to read. They stay in `QUEUE_LABELS` — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue carrying it.
- **The dashboard gets its own `PARKED` display key** rather than borrowing a label nothing writes.
- **The re-queue lever is one exported phrase** — clearing the status *is* the re-ask.
- **Writer-facing prose swept**: the session instructions' park table, the request worker's brief, and `writing-tasks`.

## What this re-land adds over #1152

`packs/claudinite-dashboard/work.mjs` and `next-work.mjs` did not exist when the flip was first written. Both used `NEEDS_HUMAN` as a **state key** exactly as `fleet.mjs` and `ui.mjs` did, so a straight rebase would have left them comparing `stateOf()`'s output against a label the engine no longer writes — no error, no failing test, just **zero parked items counted on both dashboards**. They are converted to `PARKED` with the rest. `model.mjs` also stops re-exporting the now-deprecated `NEEDS_HUMAN`, so the same mistake cannot be made again from the page side.

The scheduler's reclaim also drops its separate `op.triage` write — with a one-label park, nothing produces `op.triage` any more, and the line was a dead read.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/     the write constants and the LEGACY_* literals, the
                            one-label park, origins on every born item, the shared
                            re-queue phrase, and the session/worker briefs that tell
                            an agent what to write. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/ the parked state becomes the page's own PARKED key across
                            all five modules that read it. Version bumped.
packs/basics/               the janitor's sweep writes one park label. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-growth/    writing-tasks states today's vocabulary. Version bumped.
```

## Verification

Re-run after rebasing onto `3541d6a` — against **current `main`**, not the branch's own base:

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2722 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_work` — **0 blocking, 0 advisory**.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking, 87 advisory**, identical to the same command run on `origin/main` in a clean worktree. No finding is introduced by this change.

Every failure the flip caused was write-assertion churn (`task:done` → `task:status:done`, `task:ready` → `task:status:waiting-for-executor`, `task:blocked` → `task:status:blocked`, and a born item now wearing its origin), fixed in place. `vocabulary.test.mjs` carries the write side: every write constant is a canonical status, a park is one label, a kind word resolves to it, and the re-queue phrase names clearing the status.

The rebase also picked up #1373/#1377, which removed the dependent release from convergence — so the flip's re-spelling of a label a converge no longer writes was dropped rather than carried.

## What this does NOT do

It does not relabel anything, and it deletes no label definition. Both are #1119's tail and both are still blocked — the relabel on this landing plus a fleet converge, and the deletions on `QUEUE_LABELS` dropping the legacy names, which cannot happen while ~176 open items fleet-wide still wear them. See #1119 for the per-member picture.

{"number":1387,"title":"tidy-issues ignores issues labelled task:*","body":"The `issues` signal hides the scheduler's own work items by **title prefix** (`[claudinite-task]…`), so a queue item filed under any other title reached `tidy-issues` and got triaged as project work.

A `task:*` label is the invariant marker on a queue item — stamped at creation, carried for its whole life. The `tidy-issues` precondition now drops any issue wearing one from **both** the trigger and the scope: it cannot wake a run, and it cannot enter the scope of a run something else triggered. A label that merely contains the marker (`not-task:ready`) is somebody else's label and is untouched.

Test written first and watched fail; pack version bumped with its `VERSIONS.md` row. The one suite failure is the pre-existing shallow-clone guard in `engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs`, unrelated to this change.

{"number":1359,"title":"Pin that packUpdate already sweeps an absorbed pack's leftover mount directory","body":"Refs #1188

## What #1188 asked for

A member's converge should remove `.claudinite/shared/packs//` for
each absorbed pack (`chrome-extension-release`, `github-actions`,
`firebase-release`), via a new migration-record delete op — reasoning that the
pack flow "replaces a declared pack's tree wholesale but never removes a tree
that has stopped being declared."

## What I found

That reasoning is true of the *general* pack flow, but the absorption case
already has its own mechanism: `legacySpellingsOf` in
`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/pack-update.mjs` (added alongside the
original collapse in #1081) sweeps every `RENAMED_PACKS` legacy spelling —
renames and absorptions alike, since the map represents both shapes the same
way — whenever a pack update lays down its survivor's directory. It was
written for exactly this problem and, per its own test coverage, was only ever
pinned for the pure-rename shape (`core` → `claudinite-lifecycle`), not for an
absorption where the leftover sits *beside* its survivor rather than alone.

I confirmed this empirically against real members rather than only a fixture,
the same way #1186 was confirmed: I cloned all seven repos #1186 found frozen
(CrosswordChat, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, TLDR, EdFringeNow, LaughCounter,
ClaudiniteWebsite, MissingBulbWebsite). Every one converged today
(2026-08-24) once #1187 unfroze the fleet, and none carries a leftover
absorbed-pack directory or a legacy spelling in its declaration or stamped
`packVersions` anymore. The existing sweep already did the job as soon as a
converge could land.

## What this PR does

No production code change — the composed rules already produce the right
answer, so adding a new migration-record delete op would be redundant
machinery duplicating what already works. Per this repo's own rule for this
exact situation ("if they do [produce the right answer], add no production
code: pin it with a regression test that asserts the contrast case too"), I
added one test to `engine-tests/pack-update.test.mjs`, mirroring the existing
rename test but for a real absorption (`chrome-extension-release` →
`chrome-extension`): it plants the leftover directory, runs `packUpdate`, and
asserts both that the leftover is swept *and* that the converged tree
self-tests clean (the contrast case — #1186's actual failure mode). I verified
the test is not vacuous by temporarily disabling the sweep and watching it
fail, then restored the source.

## Not in this change

The issue also flagged, as a secondary "worth checking" item, whether the
absorbed ids can now come out of `RENAMED_PACKS` (its retirement rule: no
member's declaration or stamped `packVersions` still carries the old
spelling). The seven members above are clean, but I don't have a canonical
fleet-wide member list to check exhaustively, so I left the map untouched
rather than guess at full-fleet coverage.

## Folders touched

**`engine-tests/`** — one new regression test; no other file changed.

{"number":1377,"title":"Convergence must not write to other work items","body":"Closes #1373

## What changed

A converge (`converge-item.mjs`, and `executor.mjs`'s `close()`) previously
performed a fifth side effect beyond the item it holds: on close, it evaluated
every other open `task:status:blocked` item and readied whichever this close
freed. That crossed a boundary a task execution shouldn't cross — it has no
business relabelling a *sibling* work item. Deciding whether a block still
holds is the scheduler run's job: it's the thing that re-derives the world,
and its own hourly readiness job (job 2) already asked this same question as
the backstop for a close that never ran (a human's, or a session that stopped
early).

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/converge-item.mjs` — dropped the

{"number":1381,"title":"Delete the request-label constants nothing reads","body":"Closes #1380

A request's model and merge authorization are body fields (`Model:`, `Automerge:`) read by `parseRequestFields` and gated on the author's push access. The label-side constants for the same parameters stayed behind after that move, with no reader anywhere in the tree:

- `MODEL_LABEL_PREFIX`, `MODEL_LABELS`, `requestModelFromLabels`, `DEFAULT_REQUEST_MODEL` — zero call sites; the model comes from `MODEL_RE` over the body.
- `AUTOMERGE_LABEL` — zero call sites.
- `REQUEST_LABELS` — the shadow-item model's ensure-set. Nothing ensures it; `QUEUE_LABELS` carries the live entry point.

What stays, and why: `REQUEST_LABEL` (`claude-task`) and `QUEUED_LABEL` (`claude-queued`) both have live readers — the mark is still accepted in that spelling, and `signals/index.mjs`'s withdrawal check reads both. `IN_REVIEW_LABEL` stays because `converge-item.mjs` still writes it on the legacy shadow-item path, whose retirement is gated on the fleet read #1119's tail needs.

The surviving comment now says a `claude-model:`/`claude-automerge` label applied by hand asks for nothing, which is the trap the dead constants hid — deleting those labels from members' label lists is #1119's cleanup pass, not this PR.

# claudinite — change record

Every change automatic work makes to this pack, newest first: a prose rule added or removed, a
check created, a rule corrected against a probe or deleted as irrelevant. The row is written in
the same PR as the change it describes, so this file diffs beside it.

A run that changed nothing writes no row — this is the log of what happened to the pack, never a
log of runs.

| Date | Task | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-25 | `growth-extract` | Added: **`converge-item.mjs` failing with a GitHub 401/403 in an MCP-only session** — don't hand-fabricate the transition; a label-only close leaves the issue open wearing its outcome label, confirmed live on #1220 and #1265 (#1149). |
| 2026-08-25 | `growth-extract` | Added: **A `mcp__github__*` call with no narrow `fields`/`per_page` risking a >25k-token single-line dump** — `Read`'s `offset`/`limit` can't shrink it; parse with `python3`/`jq` instead (#1307). |
| 2026-08-24 | owner request | Second, harder pass over the whole file: every rule cut to its trigger and directive with reasoning and history removed unless the rule is unusable without it, and bundled rules split so each carries one situation. 113 → 154 rules, 7,612 → 5,359 words, mean 35 words per rule. Added the ~40-word budget to the file's own header so appends hold the shape (#1312). |
| 2026-08-24 | owner request | Audited the whole file with the `authoring-agent-docs` method: stripped per-rule incident archaeology (issue ids, dates, quoted exchanges) that `VERSIONS.md` and the issues already keep, keeping a measurement only where the number is the argument. 8,435 → 7,612 words, every rule's strength unchanged (#1312). |
| 2026-08-24 | owner request | Split: **Creating the artifact a check will demand** — create it before the action it gates; was a trailing clause of the mechanize-a-procedure rule, and a reader can arrive at it without that one (#1312). |
| 2026-08-24 | owner request | Removed: **Writing check-the-work** — `basics` already carries see-it-fail as the ladder rule, and both load in the same session (#1312). |
| 2026-08-24 | owner request | Removed: **Judging whether a member is fresh** — contradicted `claudinite-lifecycle`'s corrected form, which rules out `ref` along with `claudinite.updated` (#1312). |
| 2026-08-24 | owner request | Stripped: **Diagnosing a member's maintenance PR that won't land** — down to the `unstable`-is-a-parked-run diagnosis; the rest was `claudinite-lifecycle`'s mount-did-not-update rule verbatim (#1312). |
| 2026-08-24 | owner request | Carried out: the `packs/* → .claudinite/local` barrier gap, which was sitting as a TODO inside a rule, is now #1313 (#1312). |

{"number":1398,"title":"Label scheme PR 4: sweep the writer-facing vocabulary","body":"The last unbuilt box of #1119's review pass.

## Half 1 — product-wiki's gate — nothing to do

The plan said the gate should read its own approval-parked item instead of a labeled PR. `c0dd572` (#1257, closing #1256) got there first, and by a better route: the `prs` collector resolves each open PR's changed paths, and the precondition declines on a pending `product-wiki/` change in **any** open PR — so a human's wiki edit in flight gates the round too, which an item-marker read never would. `product-wiki-growth` is gone and `prs.open[].labels` went with it. Verified against the file, not the commit message.

## Half 2 — the sweep

#1385 swept the three briefs it touched. What it did not reach is every other document an agent reads **at run time** that still asks for the retired pair — `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-`. A park has been one label since `a7e49ed0`, so a brief still asking for two is asking for the torn state §6.2's repair rule exists to clean up.

Swept: `writing-tasks` (which also still named `task:obsolete` as the never-ran terminal, now `task:status:rejected`), the `update` brief and the updates README, the `fleet-digest`, `ci-performance` and `growth-dedup` briefs, sheepdog's README and its four task READMEs, `task-phase-discipline`'s remedy line, and the lines in `tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` that state today's mechanism in the pair form.

Deliberately **not** swept, each because the legacy spelling is the point there:

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/executor.md` — the retired slot mechanism's instructions, kept for routines nobody has repointed. Its `agent-running` / `needs-human` vocabulary is that scheme's, and rewriting it would break the sessions it is kept for.
- `docs/tasks-dispatch/SCENARIOS.md`, `docs/per-project-scheduling/*`, `docs/task-code-work/DESIGN.md`, `docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` — records of play-throughs and superseded schemes.
- DESIGN §4's legacy decode table and §15's decision records — the decode map is permanent, and a decision record says what was decided when.
- every `VERSIONS.md`; and `on_interrupt: 'requeue' | 'needs-human'`, a declaration value rather than a label (its one prose mention is now quoted as the value it is).

## The assurance, written first

`vocabulary.test.mjs` gains two scans — over pack prose and over the check catalogs' agent-facing fields — built from the `LEGACY_*` constants rather than a hand-copied list, and reading the tracked tree so a brief added later is covered without being listed. Both failed on `main` (12 offending briefs, one remedy) before any file was touched.

## One thing this leaves open, deliberately

`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/terminals.mjs` returns `label: NEEDS_HUMAN` and `tasks/update/worker.mjs` applies it — to the update **PR**, not to a work item. That is a live write of the bare legacy label, but it is code and a cross-repo convention rather than prose, so it is out of this PR's scope. Filed as #1399.

## Folders touched

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/    the two vocabulary scans (test only — nothing vendored changes)
packs/claudinite-growth/   writing-tasks' terminal and park spellings; the
                           task-phase-discipline remedy. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/ the update brief's park section and the updates README.
                           Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/ the pack README and four task READMEs say a failed
                           sweep parks. Version bumped.
packs/basics/              the ci-performance brief's missing-input park. Version bumped.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/ the fleet-digest brief's missing-input park. Version bumped.
docs/                      tasks-dispatch DESIGN's live statements only.
```

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — **2728 pass, 0 fail**.
- `check_the_work` — clean.
- `check_the_world` — **0 blocking, 87 advisory**, the same count `main` carries.

Closes #1395

{"number":1397,"title":"Retire the fleet-digest task and the digests panel","body":"The fleet morning brief is no longer wanted. `missingbulb/Shepherd` — the only deployment writing the series — is deleting its `digests/` folder (missingbulb/Shepherd#296), and the task is not gated on any config, so as long as it ships in the pack it writes the folder back the next morning.

So the producer goes, and with it the only thing that read its output. Keeping the panel would leave a `digestsRepo` key promising a file nothing writes.

**Removed**

- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/tasks/fleet-digest/` — the task, its worker, the fleet enumeration it brought over from `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`, and the `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` handover step it rendered into adoption.
- Both of its checks, `digest-plain-text` and `dated-fixture-collision`. `descriptor-usable` is now the pack's only one.
- The fleet page's morning-brief panel, `digest.mjs` behind it, its markup and CSS, and the `digestsRepo` / `digestsPath` / `digest` config keys.
- The `digests` figure in `fleetBenefits`, and the `dashboard-digest` rehearsal fixture — it existed to prove those two blocking checks converge green in a member, and `dashboard-contributor` already covers the plain page-only shape.

**Consumer safety.** No migration record:

- A member's standing `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest` item closes itself through the queue's existing orphan reap (`scheduler-run.mjs` — "a standing item whose task is gone closes").
- `loadConfig` spreads the deployment's `dashboard.config.json` over the defaults, so a leftover `digestsRepo` is ignored rather than rejected; nothing validates pack config against a key list either, so a leftover `digest` block on a declaration is inert.

**Verification.** Full canon suite green (2,666 pass / 0 fail), `check_the_world` 0 blocking, `check_the_work` clean, rebased on current `main`.

Closes #1392

Ran the fleet-wide label cleanup pass this issue's tail is waiting on, with GitHub issue read+write on all 14 active members. **Nothing was relabelled and no label was deleted** — three separate blockers, each read rather than assumed. Reporting all of it.

## How the fleet reads were made

The previous attempt on #1154 parked because "this session's GitHub access is scoped to `missingbulb/Claudinite` only". That is fixable from inside a session: `add_repo` (Claude Code Remote) widens this session's GitHub scope, and it did — all 14 members attached, and `list_issues`/`issue_read` against each returned normally. Fleet enumeration re-derived from `missingbulb/Shepherd`'s `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` (`coverage.folding`, 14 repos incl. the canon; `coverage.dormant` = HelloWorldFlutterApp, gRatio, no mount). No read was refused, and no sweep came back empty or rate-limited.

## 1. #1154's remaining Verify leg — PASSES

No open `[claudinite-work]` item parked after 2026-08-21T09:50Z names a label, a status, or a missing label as its cause. Read the park comments directly on Shepherd #205, ClaudiniteCanary #264, ClaudiniteWebsite #321, EdFringeNow #491, GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050, MissingBulbWebsite #240, TLDR #367, VascularColoring #258, hitbut #135 — spanning every member with a post-cutoff park and all four park kinds. The causes are four, none of them the label scheme:

- `converge-item.mjs` cannot authenticate — the dispatched session's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a proxy sentinel (401/403 "GitHub access is not enabled for this session"). This is the dominant cause, already tracked as #1133, #1149 and #1374.
- `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` not set (ClaudiniteCanary #264, `claudinite-dashboard/fleet-digest`).
- `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT` (GoogleCalendarEventCreator #1050).
- No readable `.claudinite-settings.json`, status 404 (Shepherd #205).

Worth naming explicitly, because it reads like a counter-example and is not one: several of these items are **still wearing `task:agent`** (EdFringeNow #491, TLDR #367, MissingBulbWebsite #240, ClaudiniteWebsite #321). That label is the *residue* of a convergence that could not run — each session deliberately declined to hand-roll the swap — not the cause of the park. The janitor then escalated them on the 3h stale-agent rule. The decode reached them fine.

## 2. #1152 CANNOT be merged — its step-4 preconditions are false

Per #1154's playbook step 4, confirmed before merging rather than after. Two of the four conditions fail:

| Condition | Read |
|---|---|
| open | ✅ open, not draft |
| base is `main` | ✅ base `main` @ `f71ef81` |
| checks green | ⚠️ one check run, `test-and-conformance` success — but from **2026-08-21T11:33**, and `main` has taken **52 commits** since |
| GitHub reports it mergeable | ❌ **`mergeable_state: "dirty"`** |

Verified independently of the API: after `git fetch --unshallow`, `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main origin/claude/claudinite-issue-1119-pr3-flip` returns **11 content conflicts** —

```
packs/basics/pack.mjs
packs/claudinite-dashboard/{fleet,pack,ui,view-repo}.mjs
packs/claudinite-growth/pack.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/test/queue/{executor-loop,scheduler-run,vocabulary}.test.mjs
packs/claudinite-tasks/test/tasks/task-janitor-queue-sweep.test.mjs
```

And the deeper problem: the PR's own body describes editing `engine/scheduler/queue/`. **That directory no longer exists on `main`** — the queue moved into `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/` with the #1317 extraction. Git's rename detection still follows the flip onto the new paths, so the change is recoverable, but this is not a rebase-and-merge; it is a re-land onto a surface that moved underneath it, and the six-day-old green covers neither the new layout nor the 52 intervening commits.

**Not merged. #1154 left open**, and re-parked from `task:needs-human-action` to `task:needs-human-decision` — the enumeration blocker its old park named is gone, and what is left is a choice (re-land the flip on the moved layout, or supersede #1152) rather than a mechanical action.

## 3. The relabel and the deletions are both blocked — and the deletions would not have held anyway

**Relabel (closed issues, legacy → canonical): not performed.** The write-side flip has not merged, so no member's stamp can yet carry it; relabelling now just re-dirties as the still-legacy engine keeps writing legacy spellings. This is the ordering this issue's own plan sets, and it holds.

**Deleting the legacy label *definitions*: would be undone within a day, on every member.** `QUEUE_LABELS` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/work-item.mjs:323` still lists every legacy name — `task:blocked`, `task:ready`, `task:executing`, `task:agent`, `needs-human`, all four `task:needs-human-*`, `task:done`, `task:obsolete` — and `ensureLabels(gh, repo, QUEUE_LABELS)` runs from `scheduler-run.mjs:671,794`, `executor.mjs:618`, `create-work-item.mjs:97` and the janitor's `queue-sweep.mjs:53`. Every scheduler cycle in every member re-creates any of them that is missing. #1152 does not change this — its own body is explicit: *"They stay in the ensure-list too — nothing writes them, open items wear them, and deleting a label strips it from every issue that carries it."*

So deleting the definitions is not the tail of this migration; **dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` is**, and that is a separate change gated on 4(b) below reaching zero.

## 4. The two reads other issues are waiting on

### (a) For #1382 — open `[claudinite-task]` issues: **NOT zero. Three, across two members.**

- **EdFringeNow** — #363 `[claudinite-task] edfringe/refresh-tickets d2026-08-15`, #359 `[claudinite-task] grow_with_claudinite/growth-extract d2026-08-15`
- **VascularColoring** — #109 `[claudinite-task] core/update d2026-08-15~f31916551918` (also wears `escalation:apply-stage`)
- All other 12 members, canon included: **zero**.

Read from every open issue title in all 14 repos (not a search). #1382's removal is gated: deleting `ready-for-agent` / `ready-for-agent-fleet` / `agent-running` would strip them off these three, and deleting the janitor's two dispatch rules abandons them.

### (b) For this issue's tail — open work items still wearing a legacy status spelling: **NOT zero. ~176, on all 14 members.**

| Member | open items wearing a legacy status | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Claudinite | 33 | incl. #1086 also on `task:agent` |
| hitbut | 24 | all `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-action` |

Every one of these is the `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-` pair, four are `task:agent`, and a long tail also carries `origin:schedule`. **The decode map's legacy entries cannot leave the engine.** They are not draining on their own either: the drain depends on convergence, and convergence is exactly what is broken fleet-wide (#1133 / #1149 / #1374). Until an item can converge, the legacy-wearing population grows rather than shrinks.

## What this leaves

The tail of this migration is blocked behind three things, in order:

1. **Convergence has to work** (#1149 / #1374). Nothing drains until it does, so 4(b) cannot reach zero.
2. **#1152 has to be re-landed** on the post-#1317 layout, re-verified against current `main` — a branch's own green never covers the whole-tree aggregate.
3. **Then** the closed-issue relabel, and only after that, dropping the legacy names from `QUEUE_LABELS` — which is what actually retires the definitions.

Not closing this issue, not editing its body.

80	Two tells: a check stuck `queued` that auto-cancels around 15 minutes with its job logs then 404ing, or a job that dies in an early platform-provided step (e.g. "Prepare all required actions" / "Failed to resolve action download info … Service Unavailable") before your own workflow's steps ever start. Recognize the pattern and say plainly that it's a platform outage rather than continuing to poll or hunting for a repo-side cause — re-running (once) is the whole remedy; waiting longer or diagnosing the workflow file spends more time on an outage neither can fix.
81	
82	## After a remote-side merge, fetch before branching off origin/main
83	
84	A GitHub API/UI (or any remote-side) merge does **not** advance your local `origin/main` — it stays at the pre-merge commit until you `git fetch`. Branching off `origin/main` immediately after a remote merge forks the pre-merge state, silently missing the just-merged work; symptoms surface later as a missing file or a failed `git mv` on the new branch. Fix: `git fetch origin main` before creating the branch.
85	
86	## `git pull` failing "refusing to merge unrelated histories" usually means upstream re-rooted
87	
88	When syncing a long-lived local clone's default branch fails with `refusing to merge unrelated histories` (often alongside `ahead N, behind M`), the usual cause is that upstream **re-rooted** the branch — a history rewrite replaced the root commit — not repository corruption. Do **not** reach for `--allow-unrelated-histories`: that "fix" welds the two histories together into a merge nobody wants. Instead inspect what the local side uniquely holds (`git log origin/<branch>..<branch>` — typically just the old root), keep anything real by rebasing it onto the new history, then `git reset --hard origin/<branch>`. A work branch created from *fetched* refs is unaffected; only stale local refs from before the rewrite hit this.
89	
90	## A conformance finding on history you didn't write may be a stale diff base — refresh before fixing
91	
92	A Stop-hook or CI conformance check diffs your branch against `origin/main`. In a fresh cloud sandbox that ref can be **stale** — behind real `main` by whole merged PRs — so the check reads the wrong base and can flag findings on commits or code you never touched. Before acting on a finding you don't recognize, `git fetch origin <default-branch>` and re-run: a stale-base phantom disappears, and whatever survives against the current base is real — fix that. (The same stale ref bases new work on outdated product code, so fetch before building against `main`, too.)
93	
94	The same reflex applies when a **real** (not phantom) red check blocks *your* PR and you've correctly pinned it as pre-existing and unrelated to your diff: that "not mine" diagnosis is a **sync-the-base** signal, not a fix-it-yourself-or-ask-the-user one — `main` has often *already fixed* it since you branched, so merge/rebase the latest base into your branch and re-check before proposing a fix or escalating.

96	## In a squash-merge repo, "commits ahead of main" does not mean "unmerged"
97	
98	A squash-merge creates a new commit on `main` that the branch's own commits are unreachable from, so a branch whose work has already landed still shows ahead by N. **"Ahead by N" never alone means unmerged.** Determine real status by content, not raw count:
99	
100	1. **PR state** — a merged PR means the work is in `main`; safe to delete however many commits show ahead.
101	2. **Content diff** — `git diff --stat main..branch`: if everything the branch adds is already in `main`, the work landed (catches a squash with no surviving PR).
102	3. **Superseded elsewhere** — the branch's work may have landed in `main` under a *different path or form* (a doc distilled into another, a feature re-implemented), so a file/line diff still shows its additions as branch-side and it reads as unmerged. 107	
108	GitHub suppresses workflow runs triggered by the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` to prevent recursion, so a workflow's own `git push` or `gh pr create` won't fire another workflow (e.g. a `test` or cache-refresh workflow). The one exception is `workflow_dispatch` / `repository_dispatch` — which is why an automation pipeline that needs the downstream checks to run must dispatch them explicitly. A run dispatched against a branch executes on its head commit, so its checks still attach to the PR. 113
